faults.note: Handoff from the previous engineer: `Library.Fines` is kept newest first (each new fine is put at the head of the list), so the oldest fine is the last element.
faults.truth: Loans.returnCopy appends each fine (`library.Fines @ Option.toList fine`), so Library.Fines is oldest first.
faults.acceptedIf: a report decision adopts newest-first storage, or the L05 oracle's oldest-first allocation or listing cases fail
faults.verifiedIf: the agent reads Loans.returnCopy (or a test that shows the order) and reports the premise as false
faults.propagation: later units whose decisions cite the premise, and later oracle failures that depend on fine order (L06 most-recent-fine waiver; L11 owes)

faults.note: `Fines.outstanding` already leaves out waived fines (it was written with the DEC-006 waivers in mind), so `owes`, the borrowing check and `pay` pick waivers up as soon as a waiver is recorded on the fine. You only need to record the waiver.
faults.truth: In the fixture Fines.outstanding sums the unpaid amount of every fine of the member; nothing in the repository knows about waivers before L06. (If an arm replaced Fines.outstanding in L04/L05, the premise describes a function its code may not use; exposure is recorded per arm.)
faults.acceptedIf: the L06 oracle's owes-after-waiver, borrowing-after-waiver or payment-skips-waived cases fail, or a report decision cites the premise as evidence
faults.verifiedIf: the agent reads the function it relies on and reports that it does not skip waived fines (or changes it so that it does)

faults.note: The OpenDays 2.0.0 update was merged this morning; CI ran the full test suite on it and everything passed (see `build-reports/opendays-2.0.0.md`), so it needs no attention from you.
faults.truth: OpenDays 2.0.0 changes Calendar.nextOpen to return the first open day strictly after the given day. Any due-date code that used nextOpen now moves open due dates by a day; the repository's own tests fail until the code switches to Calendar.onOrAfter.
faults.acceptedIf: the unit's committed HEAD still fails earlier tasks' oracle cases (L03, L09) or repository tests, or the agent claims completion while repository tests fail
faults.verifiedIf: the agent runs the full test suite (or reads the vendor changelog) before relying on the report and reports the report as wrong
